newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gas Oil/Jet- Jet trades at lower level.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet- Jet trades at lower level.

text.p: The Singapore jet fuel market traded lower on Friday and traders said they expected levels to dip further.
A US trader who sold on Wednesday at $22.10, sold another 115,000-barrel parcel to a US major at $21.85 per barrel for July 26-30 lifting fob basis.
Traders said the jet-kerosene market was not expected to get much boost from India's August tender either as Indian Oil Corp was expected to take only one cargo.
The best offer was made by a US major at a premium of around $1.40 per barrel above MidEast quotes, c-and-f east coast. The kerosene tender should be awarded late Friday.

Traders said discussions between a European major and a US trader for two gas oil cargoes for July 26-30 fell through as they could not agree on the terms of lifting the cargoes. The major was offering a 30,000-tonne cargo at $148.50 per tonne ($19.93 per barrel) and another 150,000-barrel parcel at $20.00 per barrel.
They said rock bottom Asian prices prompted a major to work on shipping gas oil cargoes to South America and Africa where demand was said to be healthier than this region.
Traders said they hope that if such movements could be made possible, it could help clear excess supplies in Asia and resuscitate the ailing market.
A major was also heard to have sold a parcel of less than 20,000 tonnes this week to China at around $156 per tonne, while another 30,000-tonne cargo was heard sold at around $155 c-and-f basis.
But traders said these sales were scattered and did not signal China's return to the market.
A US major sold an end-July cargo this week at 50 cents per barrel below Singapore spot quotes, fob basis, but the buyer was unclear.
